publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electrostatic discharge (ESD) penetration process is considered in systems terms; the ESD source acts as the input to the enclosure; which is the system. The system is characterized by the application of the generalized wave equation to a multilayer plate. It is shown that the generalized wave equation reduces to a vector diffusion equation for conductive enclosures, but that both its wave and diffusion parts must be considered for enclosure containing dielectric layers. The advantages of the systems approach are discussed. It is shown that the system input can, without loss of generality, be considered an impulse. The impulse response can be obtained by the inverse fast Fourier transform (FFT) of the steady-state frequency response, which itself can be determined using harmonic analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-premises emission testing of digital switching systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A procedure that has been successfully used for on-premises testing of telephone switching systems with time-division networks is described. Procedures and special test equipment that have been developed during the past seven years while testing nearly 30 different sites are described. Tools for separating equipment-under-test (EUT) emissions from ambient emissions include a customized, frequency-comb generator that simulates signals from the EUT. Compliance determination using on-premises testing has proved both practical and feasible. The procedure is also useful for identifying major emission sources and possible areas of equipment improvement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Absorber lined open area test site-a new type of EMC test facility
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An alternative compatibility (EMC) test facility is proposed and investigated that has only one radio-frequency (RF) absorber-covered surface, the ground plane itself. The use of an absorber-line site alleviates such serious flaws of existing EMC test facilities as variable product/sensor separation distance, incomplete elevation-angle coverage, and reference ground-plane uncertainty. These problems are examined, the absorber-lined site is described, and experimental verification of its effectiveness is provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fields at a radiation measuring site
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A study of the peculiar nature of electromagnetic fields encountered when measuring at short distances over the entire frequency range of 30 to 1000 MHz is presented to help avoid gross mistakes in the measurement, as well as in the interpretation, of results. A discussion of the mechanisms that cause the observed effects is included, along with a proposal for possible improvement of current measuring practice. A list of publications facilitating further study of the subject is included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Review of EMC practice for launch vehicle systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Case histories, design and test practice in the field of advanced electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) are reviewed. Failures caused by lightning, electrostatic discharge (ESD), and electromagnetic interference (EMI) and radiofrequency interference (RFI) are discussed. System and equipment design and analysis are examined, including lightning and ESD protection and computer-aided EMC analysis. Testing of a number of rockets and spacecraft is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectrum conservation and economic tradeoffs
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Economic and engineering tradeoffs of spectrum conservation techniques are discussed. Preferred methods of encouraging more intensive use of the spectrum are those that result in greater service flexibility and responsiveness to changing supply and demand conditions. Specific examples are discussed, including provision for the rendition of services secondary to the primary allocation, the use of flexible rather than rigid technical standards, more accurate propagation models, interference protection criteria based on actual equipment performance, and privately negotiated interference agreements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
